system_architecture.description: Self-powered CSF pressure/flow sensor powered by harvested mechanical energy from CSF pulsations or catheter motion. R1 fix: original P-15 assumed unrealistic power density; R1 redesign uses piezoelectric transducer with rectifier + storage + duty-cycled sensing.

subsystems.name: Piezoelectric transducer (PVDF or PZT)
subsystems.function: Converts mechanical strain (CSF pulsation, catheter motion) to electrical charge via piezoelectric effect

subsystems.name: Power conditioning (rectifier + boost + storage)
subsystems.function: AC->DC rectification, voltage boost, energy storage in capacitor or thin-film battery

subsystems.name: Duty-cycled sensor (pressure or flow)
subsystems.function: Measures ICP or flow at low duty cycle (e.g., 1 measurement per minute) compatible with harvested energy budget

subsystems.name: Wireless data transmitter (passive RFID or backscatter)
subsystems.function: Transmits measurement to external reader without requiring onboard power for active RF

key_equations: P ~ (d33 * g33 * sigma^2 * Volume) / (2 * duty_cycle) [piezo harvested power]
energy_budget.input_energy_source: CSF pulsation (~1 Hz cardiac-driven) and/or catheter motion (postural)
energy_budget.expected_power_density: EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT: published piezo harvesters yield 0.1-10 μW/cm^3 depending on strain amplitude (PMC11434573, ACS Appl Energy Mater)
energy_budget.R1_correction: Original P-15 assumed power density sufficient for continuous sensing; R1 redesign uses duty-cycled sensing with harvested energy budget
energy_budget.critical_parameter: Mechanical-to-electrical conversion efficiency; duty cycle compatible with energy budget

mechanism_architecture.physical_changes: Mechanical strain deforms piezoelectric transducer, generating charge Q = d33 * F (force) or V = g33 * d * sigma (stress); rectified and stored; sensor sampled at duty cycle
mechanism_architecture.key_physics: Piezoelectric effect in PVDF or PZT: charge generated proportional to applied stress. Power output P ~ (d33 * g33 * sigma^2 * Volume) / (2 * cycle_time), scales with stress squared and active volume.

energy_model.input: Mechanical strain time-series sigma(t) from CSF pulsation (1 Hz) or motion (postural)
energy_model.model: P_avg = (d33 * g33 * sigma_rms^2 * Volume) / (2 * T_cycle) * eta_rectification
energy_model.power_budget: Sensor: ~10 μW active, 0.1 μW standby; if duty cycle = 1%, avg = 0.1 μW + 0.099 μW = ~0.2 μW

governing_model.summary: Piezoelectric energy harvesting from low-frequency mechanical strain. Power output scales with stress squared, active volume, and material coupling coefficient. Duty-cycled sensing matches available power.

P_avg = (d33 * g33 * sigma_rms^2 * Volume * eta) / (2 * T_cycle)
assumptions: CSF pulsation provides reliable 1 Hz strain source (literature-supported for cardiac-driven ICP waveform)
PVDF or PZT retains piezoelectric properties in implant environment (UNKNOWN for chronic)
Rectification efficiency 50-80% achievable at low voltage (EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT)
Energy storage leakage negligible over measurement cycle (UNKNOWN for implantable capacitors)
Sensor active power target ~10 μW (EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT for low-power medical sensors)
boundary_conditions: Strain amplitude: ~10-100 με typical for physiologic motion (EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT)
parameter_sensitivities: sigma (stress) — power scales as sigma^2; 2x stress = 4x power
d33 * g33 (material coupling) — PVDF: 33e-12 * 0.216 = 7.1e-12; PZT-5H: 593e-12 * 19e-3 = 1.1e-11 (PZT ~50% higher coupling but more brittle)
Volume — linear scaling with active material volume
Rectification efficiency — typically 50-80% at low voltage
Frequency — power scales linearly with frequency for impulse-like excitation
failure_regimes: Stress below threshold -> harvested power < sensor standby -> system never wakes
Piezo depoling at body temperature or due to mechanical fatigue -> d33 degrades
Capacitor leakage > harvested energy -> no net storage
Rectifier forward voltage drop > piezo output voltage -> no rectification

engineering_core.external_precedent: EXTERNAL_PRECEDENT ≠ INVENTION_VALIDATION — published piezoelectric energy harvesting literature (PMC11434573, ACS Applied Energy Materials) establishes that piezo harvesters can power low-duty-cycle sensors from mechanical strain. It does NOT establish that the proposed catheter-integrated harvester achieves sufficient power in CSF environment.
